2610.08540.title: Toward Alignment Scaling Laws: A Framework and First Preregistered Measurements
2610.08540.paper_summary: Whether alignment gets easier or harder as models grow is often argued from isolated findings, as if alignment were one property. We treat it as a family of measurable scaling relations: for each risk category r, the alignment burden needed to hold a fixed safety target is modeled as B_r(N)=a_rN^alpha_r, with N a capability proxy; against a budget proportional to N, scaling helps if alpha_r<1, keeps pace if alpha_r~1, and accumulates alignment debt if alpha_r>1. We give three operationalizations of burden and distinguish observed, audited and true alignment. A toy model, in which corrections consume capability headroom, makes the consequences explicit. We prove that the largest exponent among corrected risks, not an average, sets the long-run regime; that above 1 any policy holding headroom above a floor must grow super-exponentially; that, for burdens that are positive mixtures of power laws, fits on small models underestimate large-scale exponents; and that an audit that uncovers hidden failures without false positives never underestimates true alignment. We propose a pre-registrable protocol and apply reduced versions of it twice. A preregistered reanalysis of public adversarial-training data for Pythia classifiers finds that the compute needed to bring attack success under 10% grows as N^0.60. A preregistered pilot on Qwen2.5 0.5B-72B finds exponents of -0.05 for truthfulness and 0.48 for stated dispositions (both scaling helps under its reduced rule, though local slopes approach 1 at the top; replicated on Qwen3 0.6B-14B), while sycophancy (0.89, or 0.83 with two seeds added at 72B) and a planted backdoor are undetermined: the backdoor is removed quickly when its trigger is known but survives blind safety training at four of five sizes. We release four browser games that play these laws (www.aisafety.fun). We make no claim about which regime holds for current frontier models.
2610.08540.paper_summary_zh: 無論隨著模型的增長，對齊是否變得更容易或更困難，通常是基於孤立的發現進行爭論，就好像對齊是一個單一的特性。我們將其視為一系列可測量的縮放關係：對於每個風險類別 r，為了保持固定的安全目標，所需的對齊負擔被建模為 B_r(N)=a_rN^alpha_r，其中 N 是一個能力代理；對於與 N 成比例的預算，如果 alpha_r<1，則縮放有助於；如果 alpha_r~1，則保持步伐；如果 alpha_r>1，則累積對齊債務。我們提供三種負擔的操作化，並區分觀察到的、審計的和真實的對齊。一個玩具模型，其中修正消耗能力餘量，使後果變得明確。我們證明，在修正風險中，最大的指數，而不是平均值，決定了長期制度；在 1 以上，任何保持餘量高於底線的政策必須以超指數方式增長；對於正的混合冪律的負擔，小模型的擬合低估了大規模的指數；而揭示隱藏失敗而不產生假陽性的審計從不低估真實對齊。我們提出了一個可預註冊的協議並兩次應用其簡化版本。一項對 Pythia 分類器的公共對抗訓練數據的預註冊重分析發現，將攻擊成功率降低到 10% 所需的計算量隨著 N^0.60 增長。一項對 Qwen2.5 0.5B-72B 的預註冊試點發現，真實性指數為 -0.05，陳述的傾向為 0.48（在其簡化規則下，兩者都得到了幫助，儘管在頂部的局部斜率接近 1；在 Qwen3 0.6B-14B 上重複），而諂媚（0.89，或在 72B 時添加兩個種子為 0.83）和一個植入的後門則未確定：當觸發器已知時，後門會迅速被移除，但在五個大小中的四個中，盲安全訓練仍然存活。我們發布了四個瀏覽器遊戲來展示這些法則（www.aisafety.fun）。我們對當前前沿模型所持的制度不作任何聲明。
2610.08540.author: Jeremy Canale et.al.
